references.text: The Lord warns Pharaoh of the consequences of refusing to let Israel's people go free, with a threat of judgment.
Pharaoh refuses to let the people go, which is a recurring theme throughout the plagues.
The same phrasing is used: 'if you refuse to let them go' - showing the pattern in God's warnings.
The fulfillment of the threat about locusts coming over Egypt.
Locusts as God's judgment on disobedience are also mentioned in the curses in Deuteronomy.
The prophet Joel describes a plague of locusts as God's judgment, with parallels to the plague in Egypt.
The Lord mentions the locust as part of His army that He sends as judgment.
The psalm recounts the locust plague in Egypt as part of God's mighty deeds.
The locust has no king, yet advances in ordered ranks - showing the power of the locusts.
Revelation uses locusts as a symbol of God's judgment, with an allusion to the plagues of Egypt.
Both verses are direct threats of plagues within the same narrative context (the plagues in Egypt) and use identical conditional phrasing to emphasize Pharaoh's responsibility for the escalation.
The verse represents a direct continuation of the same threat structure and sequence of events (the plagues) as the source verse, where God's judgment escalates based on Pharaoh's refusal.
